name: blake2b-simd
baseline: BLAKE2b (pure-Go reference implementation, dchest/blake2b); also compared against Go stdlib crypto/sha256, crypto/sha512, crypto/sha1, crypto/md5
workload: Hashing 64B-128KB buffers per-core on amd64, using AVX2/AVX/SSE-optimized BLAKE2b compression vs a pure-Go BLAKE2b reference and vs Go's stdlib hash implementations
claimed_speedup: AVX2 up to 3.94x over pure-Go BLAKE2b at 128K blocks (approaching ~1GB/s per core); benchmark table shows BLAKE2b-simd at 850.64 MB/s vs stdlib SHA-256 at 189.58 MB/s (derived from page data: ~4.5x)
compiler_and_flags: Go toolchain (version unstated); AVX2/AVX/SSE Go assembly
hardware: Intel Xeon E5-2620 v3 @ 2.40GHz (6c/12t) for AVX2 numbers; MacBook Pro 2.7GHz Core i7 for AVX/SSE numbers
tradeoffs: amd64-only SIMD paths with generic Go fallback for other architectures; project is archived so no ongoing security maintenance; requires custom asm2plan9s toolchain for building AVX code paths
caveats: Benchmark compares against the project's own pure-Go BLAKE2b baseline and Go's stdlib hash implementations, not against OpenSSL's BLAKE2b/SHA-2/SHA-3; repo archived by GitHub, no commits since 2017; no stated Go compiler version; numbers are first-party README benchmarks with partial methodology (CPU stated, compiler version not).
found_via: Hacker News: search "blake2" show_hn (Show HN: Blake2b with SIMD instructions in Go, https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=12051334)
